S5.text:
Dan Hockenmaier (00:00:00):
One lesson I learned the hard way a bunch of times on this is that if you think about running a marketplace, you're basically like a gardener. You have to have a very light touch. If you're building a SaaS business, you're a construction worker, you're building the product and the features and selling it, and it's this very linear thing. For a marketplace, you're like messing with this ecosystem that you don't actually really understand how it works. And sometimes you might do something over here which drives this long-term effect two months later, and then you're going to be pulling your hair out two months later trying to figure out what you did over here that made that thing happen. So I think that the main advice is like to tread lightly. When you're messing with the core incentives or mechanisms of a marketplace, be very careful, particularly if you've got something that's working on playing with those variables.

answer.summary: Hockenmaier favors increasing share of wallet among existing customers: it builds depth of relationship, which signals stronger future retention and marketplace defensibility, and can make customers less likely to use competing marketplaces.

sections.heading: The tradeoff he favors
sections.content: For the example of growing GMV by either 10% more customers or 10% more of current customers’ wallet, Hockenmaier would choose the latter. He characterizes share of wallet as relationship depth rather than breadth and says he would take depth every time in a marketplace.

sections.heading: Why
sections.content: A higher share of wallet indicates a deeper customer relationship and says more about likely future retention and marketplace defensibility. It also raises LTV and makes customers less likely to multi-tenant—use another marketplace or service. He cautions that it can be hard to achieve high share of wallet on both sides of a marketplace, so a marketplace may need to choose which side is its leverage point.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately says Hockenmaier favors growing share of wallet among existing customers, describing it as depth over breadth. It gives the requested reasons—deeper relationships indicate stronger future retention and marketplace defensibility—and its added points about LTV, multi-tenanting, and choosing a leverage point are supported by the cited context.
